To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully developed the first dual layer molecularly imprinted solid phase extraction procedure (DL MISPER), for the simultaneous trace detection of dimethoat and terbuthyazine from olive oil samples.
a new sample preparation procedure based on molecular imprint technology has been developed to preconcentrate pesticide residues from olive oil samples.

a new sample preparation method has been developed based on molecular imprint technology for the simultaneous extraction, in a single procedure, of two pesticides belonging to different families (dimethoate and triazine) and the use of a new dual molecular imprinting SPE procedure (DLMISPE) for the simultaneous extraction in a single procedure of two pesticides belonging different families, dimethoate, and terbuthlazine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and improved sample preparation techniques for the trace analysis and determination of pesticides and other organic compounds in complex environmental and biological matrices.
the development of a new dual MIP SPE procedure that allows the simultaneous and selective extraction and preconcentration of pesticide residues from olive oil samples.

the development of an analytical procedure for the determination of pesticide residues in complex matrices, based on a dual molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) layer solid phase extraction (SPE) procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dual layer MISPE methodology is a promising and reliable alternative for the trace analysis in food matrices, especially for those matrices that are difficult to be treated with traditional SPE sorbents.

the DL MISPE methodology has proven to be a powerful sample preparation technique that can be successfully used for the preconcentration and trace analysis of pesticide compounds in complex olive oil matrices.
the dual MIP layer based sample preparation methodology is a promising approach to be used in the pre-concentration of pesticide residues in complex matrices, such as olive oil samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel dual pesticide residue methodology, which is based on molecular imprint technology and is capable of simultaneously preconcentrating both organophosphorus (dimethoate) and triazine (terbuthylazine) pesticide residues from olive oil samples at trace levels.
DL MISPE constitutes an innovative sample preparation procedure for the multiresidue analysis of pesticides belonging to the organophosphorus (OP) and triazine (T) classes in olive oil samples.

the dual layer molecularly imprinted polymer solid phase extraction (DL MISPE), as an analytical tool, is a powerful and versatile technique that can be applied to the trace analysis of pesticides in olive oil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DL MISPE constitutes an attractive and promising alternative to conventional analytical methodologies based on the use of MIPs as sorbents in SPE.
DL MISPE constitutes an effective sample preparation procedure that allows the simultaneous and sensitive extraction of pesticide residues from complex food matrices.
DL MISPE is a powerful sample preparation methodology that allows the trace analysis of pesticides in complex matrices such as olive oil.
